lines.text: # Hobbit Passover: Answer the Call
[Intro — Piano, soft female vocal]
Candles in the window, questions in the room,
Wisdom in the whisper, warning in the gloom.
Bread upon the table, truth upon the tongue—
The Hobbits raised a vision, now the work’s begun.
[Verse 1 — Melodic rap]
Monthly at the Salon, Dad gathered the great,
Genius minds grinding while I listened and ate.
Small kid, tall thoughts, caught sparks in the air,
They debated what was broken and what made it fair.
Professors with perspectives, poets with a plan,
History and mystery, the measure of a man.
They didn’t chase clout, they were chasing what’s true,
Asking what the blessed and the brilliant ought to do.
Matzah cracked sharply like a map of the earth,
Bitter herbs reminding us what freedom is worth.
Every cup carried memory, every question carried weight:
How can we feast freely while the hungry have to wait?
I was quiet in the corner, but the calling came clear:
Knowledge without kindness is a crown made of fear.
So we carry what they taught us, turn the lesson into labor—
No border makes a stranger, every stranger is a neighbor.
[Pre-Chorus — Female vocal]
Can you hear the children calling
Through the sirens, smoke and rain?
We can’t claim that we are free
While another wears the chain.
[Chorus — Duet]
This is a call to arms—but the arms bring aid,
Carry food through the flood, bring the light through the shade.
Bring doctors, bring water, bring shelter, bring song,
When the whole world is hurting, the whole world belongs.
From the Hobbit Passover, rise from the table,
Give what you have, do whatever you’re able.
No guns in the gathering, no glory in war—
Just hands lifting humanity higher than before.
[Verse 2 — Faster rap]
Pack medicine, meals, maps, masks in the crates,
Move fast when disaster is testing the gates.
From famine to fire, from the quake to the cold,
Let compassion move quicker than silver and gold.
Build bridges, not bases; bring blankets, not blame,
Feed families first, never market their pain.
Let the wealthy write checks, let the workers take flight,
Let the coders build systems that deliver it right.
Track every dollar, every pallet, every plane,
Cut fraud from the flow, keep relief in the lane.
Local leaders lead; we support, never steer,
Put dignity first and make every mission clear.
The Hobbits taught discussion, but discussion must deploy;
A theory can’t feed every girl and every boy.
We need wisdom with wheels, we need mercy with might,
We need thousands moving through the middle of the night.
Not conquest—coordination.
Not control—cooperation.
A global generation building bold humanitarian stations.
From Newark to Nairobi, Gaza, Haiti, Ukraine,
Wherever people suffer, we respond to the pain.
[Pre-Chorus — Female vocal]
Every candle is a promise,
Every promise needs a hand.
Freedom isn’t merely leaving—
Freedom helps another stand.
[Chorus — Duet]
This is a call to arms—but the arms bring aid,
Carry food through the flood, bring the light through the shade.
Bring doctors, bring water, bring shelter, bring song,
When the whole world is hurting, the whole world belongs.
From the Hobbit Passover, rise from the table,
Give what you have, do whatever you’re able.
No guns in the gathering, no glory in war—
Just hands lifting humanity higher than before.
[Bridge — Piano and choir]
Why is this night different?
Because tonight we decide
That no child faces hunger
While abundance waits outside.
Why do we remember?
So oppression can’t repeat.
Why do we keep asking?
So our answers grow feet.
Dayenu for the dialogue,
But dialogue isn’t done.
Dayenu for the candle—
Now we carry out the sun.
[Breakdown — Heavy bass]
Bread breaks—teams move.
Truth speaks—prove, improve.
Planes rise—aid lands.
Hope lives—helping hands.
Think deep. Move smart.
Lead strong. Keep heart.
One world. One fight:
Keep every human life in sight.
[Final Chorus — Huge duet and choir]
This is a call to arms—but the arms bring aid,
Carry hope through the horror, make the frightened feel safe.
Bring builders, bring teachers, bring shelter, bring song,
When the whole world is wounded, the whole world belongs.
From the Hobbit Passover, rise from the table,
Make mercy organized, fearless and stable.
Let brilliance serve people, let privilege restore,
Let hands lift humanity higher than before.
[Outro]
The Salon grows silent.
The candles burn low.
But the questions became marching orders:
Learn.
Lead.
Love.
Go.
